about: Quality checks, one per plugin: the version checked, when, by whom, in which SolidCraft, the result, each criterion, and the runs. The site shows them on each plugin's page and on quality/.

checked.machine: a 4-core Intel i7-4770K with 6 GB, Linux
checked.summary: Every command ran, 30 of 30 test cases.

runs.note: 30 of 30 test cases in `solidcraft-cli plugin test`.

valid.note: Every case checks the body count and volume. Bins and plates are ordinary sketches and features in a timeline folder, with the height and labels as parameters.

permissions.note: Modelling commands, its own storage and a panel. No files, no network.

release.note: MIT, README with install and use, a zip on every release.

runs.settings: Defaults; 3×2×6 with dividers, scoop, label tab and text (raised and flush), magnet and screw holes; eco and solid bins; half and custom grids; filler; a flat and a stackable lid
4×3, half cells, magnets and screws, cells left out
400×300 and 800×600 (as a long job), with magnets
runs.time: up to 76 s as a job

runs.settings: A picked bin with its settings filled in, changed and made again
Parts list, Quick buttons, Layout, Settings

notes: Also checked by hand in the desktop app: the dialogs, Edit bin filling in a picked bin's settings, and a lid sitting in a bin's stacking lip (no overlap, resting on the lip).

checked.machine: a 4-core Intel i7-4770K with 6 GB, Linux
checked.summary: Tall cabinets with doors go over the plugin's 30 s time limit, and so does Edit in a design with many cabinets. Everything else ran well.

runs.note: About 30 runs: all passed except a tall cabinet with doors and an edit in a big design, which were stopped at the 30 s limit.

valid.note: Every body closed (0 open bodies after every run). Cabinets are components with ordinary features.

permissions.note: Writes to one folder (cut lists) and reads the clock. No network.

release.note: MIT, a detailed README with an example kitchen, a zip on the release.

runs.settings: Sink base 800 mm, matched to the cabinet beside it
Wall cabinet placed above, French cleat
Inset doors, legs, overlay back, oak, a divider
Inch units: 24 × 22 × 34.5 in, ¾ in boards
**2100 mm high, 2 doors, 5 shelves** (with and without labels)
3 to 4 drawers, in a design with one cabinet
**3 to 4 drawers, in a design with nine cabinets (about 160 bodies)**
End panel on a cabinet's free side
Over three cabinets, with a sink cut-out
CSV, and PDF with cutting diagrams

checked.fix: SolidCraft stops an ordinary command after the time limit in its manifest, at most 30 s. Since SolidCraft 0.48 an entry can be a long job (`"job": true`): it may run for up to ten minutes, shows progress and can be cancelled. Making Cabinet a job, or a tall cabinet faster, would very likely be enough. The times depend on the computer; on a faster one these may pass.

checked.machine: a 4-core Intel i7-4770K with 6 GB, Linux
checked.summary: A gear with many teeth goes over the plugin's 30 s time limit: 80 teeth, which the dialog allows, can't be made.

runs.note: 9 of 11 runs passed; 80 teeth was stopped at the 30 s limit.

valid.note: One closed body per gear, made of a sketch and an extrude.

permissions.note: Only sketch and solid commands. No files, no network.

release.note: MIT, README, a zip on the release.

runs.result: refused: "the tooth comes to a point; lower the profile shift". Right to refuse, but it comes as an error inside the plugin ("Report this to its author") rather than a message about the setting

checked.fix: The time grows with the number of teeth, about 0.35 s a tooth here. Making Make gear a long job (`"job": true`, SolidCraft 0.48 and later: up to ten minutes, with progress and Cancel), or drawing one tooth and patterning it, would fix it. Reporting a pointed tooth as an invalid setting would make that message clearer.

checked.summary: The latest release holds the standalone Windows program, not the SolidCraft plugin, so there is nothing to run in SolidCraft yet.

installs.note: It installs, but adds no commands: `plugin check` says "the plugin has no runtime".

release.note: MIT and a README, but the release zip (`thread-generator-1.8.0.zip`) holds `ThreadGenerator.exe`, not the plugin the README describes.

notes: The README describes a WebAssembly plugin (**Plugins › Add thread…**, version 2.0.6 in the repository's `plugin/` folder), but no release holds it yet. When one does, it can be checked.

checked.machine: a 4-core Intel i7-4770K with 6 GB, Linux
checked.summary: Every screw with a modelled thread, the default, goes over the plugin's 30 s time limit. Without the modelled thread, and for holes only, it works.

runs.note: 21 of 22 screws were stopped at the 30 s limit, the defaults (M3×12) too. Only screws with Thread modelled off, and holes, were made.

valid.note: What was made was closed (0 open bodies).

permissions.note: Only modelling commands. No files, no network.

release.note: MIT, README, a zip for each plugin on the release.

runs.settings: **Every head**: button, countersunk, hex, pan, cheese, set screw, threaded rod
**Every drive**: hex socket, Phillips, slotted, Torx, none
**Point tip; set screw with cup tip; flipped**
Hole only, clearance with the head recessed, at a sketch point in a block

notes: The time limit stopped the run after the plugin had asked SolidCraft for the threaded body, which is why the runs took longer than 30 s before they ended.
checked.fix: The modelled thread is what takes the time. Making Make screw a long job (`"job": true`, SolidCraft 0.48 and later: up to ten minutes, with progress and Cancel) would let it finish; a simpler thread, or Thread modelled off by default, would make it fast.
